cues: Because the walls are not lignified, the cells can still stretch.
So collenchyma supports an organ that is still growing: it bends in the wind and springs back.
It sits just under the epidermis of young dicot stems, in petioles, and in the ridges of a sunflower or pumpkin stem.
Never in monocots, and rarely in roots.
